newsitem.title: NORWAY: Leif Hoegh forms world's largest reefer group.
newsitem.headline: Leif Hoegh forms world's largest reefer group.

text.p: Norwegian shipowner Leif Hoegh & Co ASA said on Wednesday it would merge operations for refrigerated carrier ships with Safmarine of South Africa and Britain's Tufton Oceanic to form the largest specialised reefer operating group in the world.

The new company, UniCool Ltd, will control a fleet of about 85 vessels, including 18 wholly-owned, with a total capacity of 36 million cubic feet, or 28 percent of all operator-controlled reefer tonnage, Leif Hoegh said in a statement.
Total assets of the new company will be about $350 million.

The merger includes all investments in reefer vessels of the three companies and their respective shareholdings in operators Universal Reefers of the Isle of Man, which is 50 percent owned by Safmarine, and Cool Carriers AB of Sweden, a joint venture between Leif Hoegh and Tufton.

"This is a strategic development that spearheads a consolidation in the sector and gives the new company added financial strength to participate in future opportunities in the reefer market," said Thor Joergen Guttormsen at Leif Hoegh.
Safmarine will take 50 percent interest in UniCool, while the existing partnership between Leif Hoegh and Tufton will hold the remaining stake.

The new group will be based in Bermuda but commercial activities will continue in the Swedish capital Stockholm under the name Cool Carriers. Commercial management of the South African operations will remain with Universal Reefers.
The merger is expected to be finalised during the first quarter 1997.
